issues.problem: Today is Oct 7 and the plan launches new product on Oct 11, mid-October (1901 W. Madison plus a commissioned mural), the home opener and the first week of November (a new parka system). Net-new apparel needs 9-12 months of lead time and a Wabash Arts Corridor mural needs commissioning, permits and artist contracts. Nothing here can ship this season as written.
issues.fix: Re-label the brief as a 2027-28 build plan. For 2026-27 limit it to what exists: heritage and current Bulls outerwear, boutique seeding of existing SKUs, and story or content work that costs no inventory (partner introductions, the documentary, fieldhouse floor talks). Put real launch dates on the 2027 Hawk Season (Nov 2027) and a spring 2027 mural.

issues.problem: The 2026-27 City Edition is locked and in production, and the brief never says which season this concept targets. Court inlays (grid lines on the sideline maple, the Madison line through center court) belong to the Bulls and United Center, which the Blackhawks share, not to Nike. The 'avoid' list also asserts what earlier City Editions did (flag and skyline) with no check against the actual sets.
issues.fix: Pitch it explicitly as the 2027-28 City Edition brief with a Bulls-and-NBA review path, and drop the court tie-in or mark it as a Bulls decision. Pull the real list of past Chicago City Editions before claiming the grid, street-sign and Sullivan ideas are unused.

issues.target: calendar[0] (Oct 11, Bulls at Nuggets / Chicago Marathon)
issues.problem: Oct 11 is a preseason road game in Denver on ESPN. Nike does not control that broadcast, so it cannot 'tease the Lights Out pieces on air', and a marathon-weekend layering drop sells to runners and out-of-towners who are not Bulls buyers. It sits at the same priority as the Cup Nights.
issues.fix: Cut the broadcast tease. If the marathon matters, make it a Michigan Avenue flagship tourist and gifting moment with existing heritage product, and confirm Nike's actual role at the marathon first. Re-anchor the Lights Out launch to the confirmed home opener, not 'date to confirm'.

issues.problem: In a building shared with the Blackhawks, 'Hawk Season' reads as hockey merchandise to anyone outside the weather joke, and the Bulls product would then invite a Blackhawks IP question. The parka itself is a category (Carhartt, North Face, Canada Goose and every local coat) where a licensed Bulls parka has to beat the coat fans already own, and the KPI of 'share against Fanatics-run assortments' is muddled.
issues.fix: Rename it around the walk or the wind that only locals say (for example the Ashland walk or lake wind) and keep 'Hawk' to the copy. Define the parka as a coat worn over a jersey with proof of function (wear-test with season-ticket holders), and set the KPI as sell-through by price tier.

issues.problem: The brief blends two things: the 1967 Wall of Respect, made by the OBAC Visual Arts Workshop, which showed real Black heroes and no longer exists, and AfriCOBRA, formed afterward with its own founders, estates and a codified color and lettering aesthetic. A tee made on 'AfriCOBRA principles' without named artists is lifting a movement's style. Wall of Respect portraits also carry likeness rights, and a February-only launch risks reading as a seasonal Black History Month grab by a brand that has no art-world track record here.
issues.fix: License or commission named living AfriCOBRA members and estates (and the South Side Community Art Center's guidance) with a revenue share and billing on the product, or drop the capsule. Never reproduce Wall of Respect portraits. Pair it with year-round funding, not a one-month drop, and have the artists set the launch date.

issues.target: opportunities[fieldhouse-public-league] / partners (Chicago Park District, CPS, IHSA)
issues.problem: Public agencies and school bodies move slowly and restrict commercial use: Park District co-branding and floor refurbishments need board-level approval, CPS and IHSA both limit how student-athlete names and school marks are used in advertising, and a Nike-funded documentary following minors adds consent and eligibility questions. Mixing Mac Irvin Fire (a Nike-sponsored club program) into a Public League story also blurs two different ecosystems that locals do not blur.
issues.fix: Sequence it: a donation-led floor refurbishment first with no product on the floor, licensed school shirts only where a school or athletic department signs, and a documentary that follows a program with the school's, parents' and IHSA's clearance. Keep Mac Irvin Fire as the wear-test and Combine Week partner only.

issues.problem: Area-code tees are the most crowded local-shirt idea in Chicago, and 312 and 773 are already owned by indie shops and street vendors. The 630 and 847 editions risk looking like a suburban mall gimmick, and the insight about sides and grid numbers is stronger than the codes.
issues.fix: Lead with the grid-coordinate and street-sign graphics, which are Bulls-specific, and keep area codes as one entry-priced add-on. Give 708 the real South Suburb treatment, made with a south-suburb maker, and drop 630 and 847 unless a suburban partner asks for them.

issues.target: opportunities[lights-out-opener] 'Rebuild Mixtape' tee and two-player select-screen tees
issues.problem: The brief warns that a skeptical fan base will mock rebuild hype, then puts the word 'Rebuild' on a tee and prices a 31-51 team's pain. The select-screen duo tee leans on NBA Jam art (a Midway and Warner Bros. IP) and the roster-as-mixtape idea needs NBPA group licensing for three players, one a rookie, while the real insight in the arcade idea was that NBA Jam's Bulls had no Jordan.
issues.fix: Retitle the tee without 'Rebuild' (a tracklist of the roster's numbers works without the word). Draw original dot-matrix numerals and get NBPA clearance before concepting any player-pair tee. Keep the NBA Jam link in the story, not in the artwork.

issues.problem: A 'South Side chef series' with a patch tee has no basketball or uniform hook, and Black-owned restaurant partners could read as the brand borrowing their trade dress, which the food dossier warned against. It fills a calendar gap more than it follows an insight.
issues.fix: Cut the patch tee. If it stays, make it a paid event or fund for the restaurants with no Nike branding on their goods, and run it only if the owners ask for it.

issues.problem: A Chosen Few capsule 'released at the July picnic' only works as a Bulls or NBA product if the team and league license sign off, and house heritage is not a Bulls property. Selling it as both a Nike lifestyle line and Bulls product would confuse who is getting credit and money.
issues.fix: Decide the lane up front: either a Nike-credited collaboration with no NBA marks, or a Bulls-licensed piece approved by the Bulls and the NBA. In both cases name the Chosen Few DJs on the product, share revenue, and let them set dates around the picnic.

issues.target: partners (National Museum of Mexican Art, Pilsen muralist) / risks
issues.problem: Naming a living muralist (Hector Duarte) and a Pilsen launch in a strategy document puts a neighborhood under federal immigration enforcement in a brand story before anyone has agreed. A brand drop in Pilsen also carries gentrification optics that the art dossier flagged, and the brief gives it a low priority and no calendar slot.
issues.fix: Remove named individuals until they agree. Fund Pilsen and Little Village institutions with no product launch or crowd event, and decide Noche Latina only after talking to the museum and artists about timing and safety.

issues.problem: Matas Buzelis is the one Chicago-born face of the rebuild and Lithuanian-American, and Chicago has a deep Lithuanian community and a basketball-obsessed Lithuania behind it. The brief mentions him in an insight and a verify line but builds no activation, despite the food dossier asking for a community night with Lithuanian bakeries and organizations.
issues.fix: Add a Buzelis lane built with his family's blessing and Lithuanian-Chicago groups (Lithuanian Plaza, Balzekas Museum, community schools): a fall community night and a small paid collaboration. Confirm his ties first, and do not tie Lithuanian national symbols to Nike product without Lithuanian federation clearance.

issues.problem: Four strong dossier ideas never reach an opportunity: Chicago Imagist art (a Chicago-only visual language for a long, gangly roster), JB skating and the rink as a Bulls track suit, Nike SB and Wicker Park skate culture, and queer nightlife from Northalsted to South Shore. The rink only appears as a partner entry.
issues.fix: Promote the JB-rink track suit to its own opportunity, because it has real uniqueness, an authentic community partner and a ready silhouette. Use Imagism as the art direction for the Zero Point sideline graphics, and state a reason for leaving out skate and Pride rather than dropping them silently.

issues.target: calendar[11] (Bud Billiken / Frankie Knuckles Day / Labor Day ARC)
issues.problem: The summer plan stacks three community moments with Bulls product during the dead zone, but two of them (Bud Billiken parade, Frankie Knuckles Day) are community events where a brand drop can look like selling on someone else's day, and Bulls-branded back-to-school products need licensing for the parade's organizers.
issues.fix: Choose one summer anchor (Bud Billiken back-to-school gifts through Chicago Defender Charities). Put Frankie Knuckles Day in the hands of the house partners and keep Nike out of it unless invited.

issues.problem: 'EST. 1939' reads like the date the phrase 'March Madness' was coined by an IHSA official, not the start of the state boys' tournament, which began in 1908. The IHSA also splits into classes with several sites, so 'Downstate' is not one bracket.
issues.fix: Use the correct 1908 tournament date or drop the date entirely. Get IHSA permission before any bracket, and check the classes and finals sites for 2027.

issues.problem: The brief calls the Cup 'the only guaranteed branded-night slate', but the Bulls play only four group games, probably two at home, and the Cup uses the league's regular uniforms with Cup court graphics that the NBA owns. A Bulls-specific Cup product story has little to hang on.
issues.fix: Treat the Cup as a watch-party and gifting tie-in in the Friday slots, and plan the two home games once the schedule is out. Skip any Cup-specific Bulls apparel claim.

issues.problem: A brown honorary-sign tab 'saluting Chicago hoops' could be read as a memorial to a specific person. The honorary-sign system exists for named individuals, and the hoops dossier calls Benji Wilson's story off-limits for product. The tab is also hard to place within NBA uniform marking rules.
issues.fix: Make the tab generic to the street grid, not an honoree, and drop it from the on-court uniform unless the league's marking rules and the Bulls approve it.

strengths: The Madison Street and grid idea passes the swap test: 1901 W. Madison, State-and-Madison zero point, North/South split and the Cubs-Sox sides all belong only to Chicago and give a uniform with a story that does not need Jordan.

It treats heritage and Jordan Brand correctly, as an evergreen layer for Jordan Brand to own, and names the rival-brand hometown heroes (Rose, Parker, Reese, Freshgoods) plus the 'Chicago' colorway as areas to avoid.
Hawk-season outerwear is grounded in the cold, the walk to the arena and the winter spending peak, and the price ladder against the 10.25% tax is realistic.

The risk register is specific on drill and gang-nation symbols, trademarked phrases (March Madness, Three-Peat, the intro song) and the Black-built origins of house, JB skating and AfriCOBRA, with paid and credited co-authorship stated.

The partner list (Chosen Few DJs, Mac Irvin Fire, Park District, Notre, South Side Community Art Center, The Rink, Chicago Defender Charities) is made of real local institutions rather than tourist-guide names.
summary: Strong on specificity and respect: the Madison Street grid and Hawk-season ideas are Chicago-only, the partner list is real and the risks name the right traps. It fails on realism and on a few community cues. Today is Oct 7 and the plan launches new product within days, so it needs reframing as a 2027-28 plan with a thin 2026-27 seeding layer. The AfriCOBRA and Wall of Respect capsule needs named, paid artists, and Buzelis's Lithuanian-Chicago lane and the JB rink suit deserve promotion over weaker items such as the chef series and 630/847 area-code tees. Several licensing paths (Park District, CPS, IHSA, NBPA, the Bulls and NBA for court and City Edition) are assumed rather than planned.
